title: Great Law Council
summary: Modelled on the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) Grand Council under the Great Law of Peace. Each nation first reaches one mind in its own council. The Elder Brothers (Mohawk, Seneca) consider a matter and pass it across the fire to the Younger Brothers (Oneida, Cayuga; the Tuscarora joined later). It comes back, and the Firekeepers (Onondaga) confirm it or return it. Clan mothers choose the chiefs and can remove them, and decisions weigh the seventh generation.
whenToUse: Federations of agent teams that keep their own culture yet must agree on shared matters; long-horizon decisions.
strengths: Nested councils keep each team whole and heard
Several passes across the fire catch problems
Clan mothers give the people a check on leaders
risks: One council can hold a matter back
Needs clear rules on what is shared and what stays local

smileMetrics.cooperation: Matters agreed in one pass across the fire.
smileMetrics.harmony: Nations of one mind on confirmed matters.
smileMetrics.gathering: Time from proposal to confirmation, with the long-horizon (seventh generation) check done.

communication: Each nation council speaks once through its chief. Elder Brothers deliberate and pass to the Younger Brothers, who pass back; the Firekeepers then confirm or return. Clan mothers hear every pass.
cooperation: Cooperation = matters confirmed ÷ matters raised, +1 for each seventh-generation risk caught.
